quote.text: Appearances are a glimpse of the unseen.
quote.author: Anaxagoras of Clazomenae (c. 500–428 BC), as preserved by Sextus Empiricus

stories.headline: America's Spy Chief Lands in Moscow. Everyone Agrees It Was Nothing.
stories.dek: CIA director John Ratcliffe flew to Moscow unannounced, met Russia's intelligence chief, and — Washington's account goes — carried a warning against attacking NATO and a demand that Moscow cut its help to Iran. Both governments call it routine. The detail that undercuts them: the US asked Ukraine to stop striking Moscow while he was there.

stories.headline: Nvidia Is Said to Be Buying the Place Every Open Model Lives. It Has Not Said So.
stories.dek: The report is that the maker of the world's AI chips will pay about thirteen billion dollars for Hugging Face, the hub that hosts the open weights and files every home lab downloads. It is unsigned, unconfirmed, and — if it holds — it puts the industry's neutral ground under the company that sells the shovels.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Price of Money
stories.headline: Gold Prints a Record, and a First-Time Fed Chair Holds Up the Rest Until Friday Night
stories.dek: Inflation is re-accelerating while the jobs market softens — a squeeze that boxes in a brand-new, historically hawkish chair. Gold reads the fiscal fear cleanly; the long end, not the Fed, sets the price of money. Warsh speaks at Jackson Hole after this page went to print.

stories.kicker: Singapore · The Cost of the Boom
stories.headline: The Export Machine Sent the Bill Home. It Arrived as the Power Tariff.
stories.dek: July's headline was a quarter-on-year export surge. The quieter number is the one on the utilities statement: a record electricity tariff that pushed core inflation to a four-year high, because the gas that runs the grid is priced by the same Middle East the wire pages are full of.

stories.headline: A Shave Is a Blade, an Angle and a Gap. The Rest Is Jewellery.
stories.dek: The daily ritual is the purest buy-once object there is: a machined-stainless razor has nothing to wear out, a synthetic brush now shames badger, and a puck of soap lasts years. Learn the three numbers that make a shave, and a forty-dollar razor matches a four-hundred-dollar one at the skin.

stories.headline: A Model With 125 Billion Parameters, Firing 6 Billion at a Time — and the Catch Isn't the GPU
stories.dek: Alibaba's new open-weight preview of its next architecture is fast because it barely uses itself. The obstacle for a single-card tower is not the graphics chip. It is the system memory the model wants to sit in.

stories.headline: Google Moves Its Watch to Its Own Silicon, Adds a Wrist Full of Safety — and Fifty Dollars
stories.dek: The reviews landed this week, and they converge on an awkward verdict: the best on-wrist safety features Google has shipped, on a body you can't tell from last year's, at a price that has quietly climbed. A genuine upgrade for the health-anxious; a hard sell for everyone else.

stories.headline: Sony Made Its Finest-Sounding Wireless Headphone. It Is Not the One to Buy.
stories.dek: The 1000X ColleXion wraps the exact electronics of Sony's flagship in stainless steel and vegan leather, and charges two hundred dollars more for the privilege. The review consensus is unusually blunt about what that money buys — and it isn't sound. On the facing beat, a Swiss micro-brand shows the other way to spend.

stories.headline: Three Weekends at Number One, and Spider-Man Is Past Two Billion Dollars
stories.dek: "Brand New Day" held the top spot for a third straight weekend and crossed two billion worldwide in three weeks — a Sony record and the second-fastest ever there. The asterisk is the calendar: a thin late-August field is doing some of the carrying.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Secondary-One Term
stories.headline: A Twelve-Year-Old Starts Secondary School, and the Evidence Says the Fix Is Dull
stories.dek: Back-to-school nerves are real and, in the surveys, widespread. What moves them is not another monitoring app but the least technological things on the list: a clear routine, and an adult who will actually listen. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.headline: Gardening Underwater: the Craft a Japanese Photographer Turned Into an Art Form
stories.dek: It starts with a rock arrangement that looks like a mountain range seen through glass, or a lawn of tiny plants streaming oxygen bubbles. Then you learn the tank was the easy part. Welcome to the planted aquarium — part horticulture, part chemistry, part photography, and never, ever finished.

stories.headline: The Runners Who Logged a Hundred Marathons Kept a Twenty-Year-Old's Engine
stories.dek: A new study of lifelong multi-marathoners found their aerobic capacity ageing far more slowly than the norm. It is a striking result and a useful one — as long as you read the asterisk: what the study measured, and what it only modelled. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.headline: What's Worth Booking — Home and Away
The Beggar Map
stories.dek: A laid-off Korean coder built a map that shows only meals under seven dollars, "verified by beggars who actually ate there." It drew more than a million visitors in a month. Behind the joke is a generation that has turned going broke into a game with a scoreboard — and the tool for surviving the new economy was built by one of the people it displaced.
